key.desc: which item; empty = the current item

action.desc: pass | ok | ng | keep | skip | retime | recheck

code.desc: ok | ng | unknown | empty -- what flow.checkpoint should write

Under DryRun or without a console the default is taken and reported with auto=true.

filled.desc: rows whose blank cell was filled

kept.desc: run.timeWindow was already set (-TimeWindow or a resume): returned as is, nobody asked

timeWindow.desc: { from; to } ISO when kind is timeWindow, else null

value.desc: the answer as text (a time in `format`; a window as "from..to")

with.message: Copy the Teams start message of the job and press Enter

message.desc: what to copy (shown on the panel)

sets.desc: @{ n (0 = shown, not pickable); id; label; names; notes (name -> text); default } (table.day_sets)

hold.desc: names the operator put on hold (h ...)

picked.desc: the picked names, in set order

message.desc: what the operator must have ready before continuing

where.desc: where to paste, for the prompt

Dry run / no console answers Enter. With front, the matching window (the frontmost one when several match) comes to the front after the panel is drawn; paste there, then answer back in the console. No match = a warning, the console stays in front. Foreground is the console afterwards.

action.desc: short verb, e.g. captured, verdict, delivered

key.desc: the item; empty = the current item, if any

progress.status.summary: Print done / pending / ng counts per field as an ASCII table

saveAs.desc: PNG path; relative paths resolve under the work dir

saveAs.desc: PNG path; relative paths resolve under the work dir; parent dirs are created

path.desc: the file that was written (absolute)

screen.capture_window.summary: Save a PNG screenshot of the window held in a session resource

b.desc: the picture compared with it (a path or a list)

okMax.desc: score at or below this = the same (10/21: the same job read 9.25 on RJODWDBC)

saveBase.desc: also save what was compared: <saveBase>.a.png (a's strip) and .b.png (the best place in b); empty = none

alert.desc: the reason when code is not ok, else empty

path.desc: the file that was written

mergeGap.desc: blank rows a band may contain

yTo.desc: 0 = the bottom; negative = that many px above the bottom

bands.desc: @{ top; bottom; height; center } in image px, top to bottom

width.desc: with state restore: resize the VISIBLE window to this (0 = keep)

title.desc: the full title of the window found

x.desc: where the window actually is afterwards

screen.fit_window.summary: Move and size a registered window to x,y width x height

argFields.desc: fields of each map passed as quoted arguments, in order

argSets.desc: one map per run (e.g. verify.pair_files pairs)

closeOthers.desc: close every window whose title contains windowTitle before each start, so the only such window is the new one

fitStepPx.desc: fine resize step near the target

fitTries.desc: resizes per capture before giving up (warning fit_failed, the capture kept)

heightEnd.desc: line rule: the visible window height for the END-view capture (a file of more than 2 x screenLines lines); 0 = height. 10/19: the HOST screen shows 17 records, so the END picture shows 17 DF lines while the first shows 16

keysFirst.desc: keys before the first capture (SendKeys syntax)

keysMid.desc: keys before the second capture of a file of screenLines+1 .. 2 x screenLines lines: the next page, so it starts at line screenLines+1

keysSecond.desc: keys before the second capture (the END view)

linesEnd.desc: line rule: the lines the END-view capture must show (fitStrip); 0 = screenLines

linesField.desc: field of each map holding its line count (the line rule)

nameField.desc: field naming the capture files (its file stem is used); blank = run number

plans.desc: one per argument set, in order (verify.df_ranges plans): mode align = the first picture shows first lines from the top, the second (end > 0) the END view of end lines -- the window starts at height / heightEnd moved by the difference in lines x fitPitchPx and the fit makes it exact; any other mode, or none, = the line rule

reuse.desc: shots of an earlier call for the same argument sets (track.json dfShots): a set whose earlier pictures exist and show the lines wanted now (firstLines / lastLines) is not run again

screenLines.desc: data lines one capture shows; > 0 switches to the line rule: lines <= screenLines one capture, <= 2 x screenLines the second capture after keysMid, more after keysSecond

secondField.desc: field that is true when a second capture is wanted

settleMs.desc: wait after the window appears / after keys

width.desc: visible window width; 0 = leave as the program opens it

windowTitle.desc: fallback when the started process shows no window of its own (a launcher / single-instance program): the top-level window whose title contains this

The program is closed with WM_CLOSE and killed if it is still there 3 s later; a capture already saved is kept either way. With fitStrip, a height that had to change is carried to the next captures of the same call, and a capture that could not be fitted is kept with warning fit_failed (look at it before review).

shots.desc: @{ first; last; name; firstLines; lastLines; firstHeight; lastHeight; reused; aligned } per run (last empty when no second capture; *Lines = text lines counted by the fit, -1 when not fitted; reused = the earlier shot was kept; aligned = a plan of mode align was followed)

screen.launch_capture.summary: Run a program per argument set, capture its window (and again after keys), close it

bands.desc: screen.find_ink_rows bands of the entry column

height.desc: box height for one row, px

lastRowCenterY.desc: fallback when bands is empty: centre of the last row, px

names.desc: every entry of the list in page order (parsed page text)

missing.desc: targets not among names, or above the top of the picture

rects.desc: @{ x; y; w; h; names } in image px

path.desc: the PNG to read; relative paths resolve under the work dir. Empty = nothing to read (an earlier export that did not happen): ok, available=false, no warning

available.desc: false: OCR could not run here (the text is empty for that reason, not because the picture is blank)

language.desc: the recognizer that read it; empty when none ran

lines.desc: the lines OCR found, top to bottom

text.desc: every line, joined with a newline; empty when nothing was read

screen.ocr.summary: OCR a PNG (Windows OCR); no OCR on this PC = ok with available=false

digits.desc: digits of a line number (HOST: 6); 5..digits are accepted, OCR drops a leading 0 at times

minLines.desc: fewer numbered lines than this = not a numbered listing (ok false). 2: a 1-line file's HOST shot shows only 000001-000002 (10/21 RJODWDBC)

screen.read_line_numbers.notes: OCR look-alikes inside a number (O/o/D -> 0, I/l/| -> 1, S -> 5, B -> 8) are folded before parsing.

available.desc: false: OCR could not run on this PC (every range ok false)

ranges.desc: @{ path; ok; first; last; count; reason } per run of consecutive numbers (one per picture, two when one image holds two shots), in input order

screen.read_line_numbers.summary: OCR the line numbers at the left of each picture -> first / last / count per picture

insetX.desc: added to the window's left (a maximized window's frame sits off-screen)

top.desc: top of the region (the panel title)

window.desc: make the geometry relative to this window's top-left

skippedRows.desc: rows above first that the region also shows (they cannot be cut out)

copy.desc: copy instead of move (the source stays)

key.desc: the item key (keySafe form; a raw key is folded)

tag.desc: distinguishes several images of one key: <key>__<tag>

name.desc: the file name that was chosen

path.desc: where the image is now

screen.save.summary: Move or copy an image to <dir>/<keySafe>[__<tag>].<ext>

backDays.desc: calendar days looked back for late rows

carryField.desc: verdict column whose ok fixes the run date (gfix-recv: track; blank = the first verdict column)

extraNote.desc: extra field shown next to the key

keyField.desc: record field holding the worklist key

records.desc: one record per pickable key: the first plan row + set, the run date column, WORKDAY

sets.desc: @{ n (1.. pickable, 0 not); id; label; names; notes (name -> text); default }

key.desc: the key to find (display form for a composite key)

columns.desc: column names in file order, profile columns appended

key.desc: which row (key display form); empty = the current item

verify.assert.summary: Run a rule table over a record: ok / ng / unknown plus the message

keyField.desc: field named in the reason for a record that failed

records.desc: the records to judge (verify.filter_records / parse_text output)

rules.desc: { rules: [ { field, op, value?, else, message } ], default: ok } -- the verify.assert shape

verify.assert_each.notes: An empty list is ok (nothing failed) -- pair it with a filter step that fails not_found when the rows are missing. The same rule table as verify.assert, so a profile keeps one vocabulary of rules.

code.desc: ok | ng | unknown: the worst verdict over the records (ok when there are none)

failed.desc: @{ key; code; reason; record } per record that did not pass, in list order

reason.desc: the first failing record's key and its rule message; "" when ok

verify.assert_each.summary: Run a rule table over every record; the worst verdict wins (ng > unknown > ok)

code.desc: ok | unknown (a value on one side only)

verify.compare_sets.summary: Compare two lists as sets; ok when they hold the same values

normalize.desc: any of trim, fullwidth, thousands (applied before equal / numericEqual)

toleranceSec.desc: with timeWithinSec: how far apart two times may be

verify.crosscheck.notes: unknown is a verdict for human.gate, never a failure. Values that cannot be read as a number / time under numericEqual / timeWithinSec count as a disagreement, not as a pass.

disagreements.desc: [ { a, aValue, b, bValue }, ... ] every pair that differs

verify.crosscheck.summary: Compare the same fact from several sources; any disagreement is unknown

set.desc: @{ to; value } | @{ to; from } | @{ to; from; pattern; replace } (.NET regex, $1 / ${name} in replace), applied in order

verify.derive_fields.notes: A rule naming a field the record lacks reads it as empty. A pattern that does not match copies the value unchanged and lists it in unchanged (a warning), so a name that does not follow the rule is visible instead of silently wrong.

records.desc: copies of the input records with the fields set

unchanged.desc: "<to> <- <from>: <value>" for every rewrite whose pattern did not match (the value was copied as is)

verify.derive_fields.summary: Add fields to records: a constant, a copy, or a regex rewrite of another field

maxExtra.desc: DF lines past the HOST's last line still lined up (a trailing line the HOST does not show, or a last line OCR missed under a red box); more = not lined up

maxLines.desc: a picture asked for more lines than this is not trusted (default kept)

offset.desc: HOST line n = DF line n - offset

pairs.desc: the DF file pairs in capture order (track.json pairs: lines = the file's line count)

ranges.desc: screen.read_line_numbers ranges of the HOST pictures, sheet order

verify.df_ranges.notes: Pure. A pair with no START picture, an unreadable picture or more than two pictures keeps the default pictures, with an alert.

alert.desc: one line for the gate when a pair could not be lined up for a reason a person should check, else empty

aligned.desc: pairs whose pictures follow the HOST ranges

plans.desc: @{ mode; first; end; reason } per pair: mode align (first / end = lines the first / END picture shows; end 0 = one picture) | free (no alignment: empty lines dropped) | default (nothing to align to)

reason.desc: one line per pair, for the run log / gate

verify.df_ranges.summary: Per DF pair: the lines its first / END picture must show to match the HOST pictures

emptyOk.desc: true: nothing matching is an answer (ok, empty lists), not not_found -- e.g. the jobs the operator picked out of a list, when they picked none

expect.desc: how many records should match; -1 = any number. A different count is a warning, not a failure

expectFallback.desc: count used when expect is -1 (e.g. the send count read off the Teams message); blank or not a number = none. When both are known and differ, a warning (expect_disagree) says so and expect wins

pluck.desc: field whose value of every kept record goes to plucked

spanFrom.desc: time field whose earliest value starts span

spanTo.desc: time field whose latest value ends span (default spanFrom)

where.desc: conditions @{ field; op; value } (verify.assert ops); empty keeps all

verify.filter_records.notes: not_found when nothing matches (transient: the page may not show the new rows yet -- retry after a refresh). A condition with op within takes value = @{ from; to } (verify.time_window output). Several files of one job (FileCount 2) are several kept rows: extent, not matched, sizes the screenshot. A within condition with no window (an empty from/to, e.g. a span an earlier step could not compute) is window_missing, not "everything passes": on 10/14 an unreadable end time emptied the span and every Jenkins file matched. span_unreadable: spanFrom is set, records matched, but their times do not parse (the page's columns moved?).

extent.desc: last - first + 1: the run of list rows from the first kept record to the last (a screen region must cover them all, even when other rows sit between); 0 when none

first.desc: position of the first kept record; 0 when none

indexes.desc: their 1-based positions in the input list

last.desc: position of the last kept record; 0 when none

plucked.desc: the pluck field of each kept record

records.desc: the kept records, in list order

span.desc: @{ from; to } ISO, empty map when spanFrom is blank or nothing matched

verify.filter_records.summary: Keep the records matching every condition; positions, plucked values, time span

expect.desc: the name that must be in it, e.g. the job's J name

label.desc: what the text came from, for the reason / alert wording

pattern.desc: regex of a name-like word, for the candidates the reason lists

verify.find_token.notes: Pure. Folding is symmetric, so a correct name never fails for a look-alike; the cost is that two names differing only by a look-alike pair (O vs 0) are not told apart.

alert.desc: the reason when code is ng or a near miss, else empty: the gate draws it red

candidates.desc: name-like words read from the text (as read, upper-cased)

verify.find_token.summary: Find an expected name in OCR text, folding look-alikes; ok / ng / unknown + alert

field.desc: the record field that holds the key

key.desc: what to find (a column value, or the key display form)

timeField.desc: the record field with the time, for newest

window.desc: { from, to } ISO; with newest, a hit inside the window beats one outside

verify.match_record.notes: record_not_found is transient: the row is usually still arriving. The key input is a raw column value ({{item.<col>}}), not {{item.key}}, unless the records carry the composite key in one field.

candidates.desc: P0-R4 candidate shape when ambiguous with tieBreak none

found.desc: how many records matched the key

index.desc: 1-based position among the records; 0 when none

verify.match_record.summary: Find the record for a key; newest / first / ask on several

found.desc: browser.wait_for found: true = the window matched, keep the clock as is

records.desc: the page rows (verify.parse_text records) to look through

withinMinutes.desc: a row this close counts as "near"; farther rows are still offered, flagged

verify.nearest_time.notes: Never silent: a changed clock comes back as code unknown so the workflow's human.gate asks (Enter = use it, s = skip and rerun with the right time). Rows whose time field does not parse are ignored.

changed.desc: true when the nearest row's time replaced the given clock

clock.desc: HH:mm:ss to go on with: the given clock, or the nearest row's time

near.desc: true when the nearest row is within withinMinutes

offsetMinutes.desc: nearest - given, in whole minutes (0 when none)

reason.desc: what was proposed and how far it is from the time given

verify.nearest_time.summary: When the expected time is not on the page, propose the nearest row's time (a gate confirms)

owner.desc: the operator as the WBS writes it (e.g. a family name); empty = no owner filter

verify.owner_pattern.notes: The arrows are the full-width ones the WBS uses (U+2190 / U+2192). An owner that contains regex characters is escaped.

everyone.desc: true when owner is empty: the plan takes every owner's rows

pattern.desc: regex for an excel.read_rows where { op: matches }: the name alone, name<-other, other->name; "" (matches every cell) when owner is empty

verify.owner_pattern.summary: Build the WBS owner-cell regex for one operator (empty owner = everyone)

longOver.desc: a pair with more lines than this is flagged long (one screen shows this many)

right.desc: file.list files of the other side

verify.pair_files.notes: A file whose lines is -1 (file.list without countLines) cannot be paired by size: run file.list with countLines = true.

pairs.desc: @{ left; right; leftName; rightName; lines; long } (paths)

verify.pair_files.summary: Pair two file lists by line count and arrival order

maxWarnings.desc: unrecognised lines reported one by one up to this many, then one summary

verify.parse_text.notes: no_records is transient: the usual cause is a page still loading. A labeled grammar always yields one record; a label it could not find is a warning (label_missing) with the field blank, and verify.assert's present/empty rules decide what that means.

names.desc: the "key" field of every record when the grammar has one (for table.key)

unrecognized.desc: non-blank lines the grammar did not recognise

verify.parse_text.summary: Parse page text into records with a delimited / labeled / columns / regex grammar

files.desc: file.download / file.list files (lines per file, arrival order); empty = parse only

headerLines.desc: a file may have this many lines more than its record count (a header)

label.desc: text before the counts in suffix (e.g. the words for "received data:")

shortOk.desc: a file with fewer lines than its count is expected (the HOST counts a header / empty lines the file does not carry): still shown lines(count), but no warning and matched stays true

text.desc: the counts as the message writes them (numbers, any separators, a unit after each); empty = no message

unit.desc: text after each count (the message's counter word)

verify.record_counts.notes: A disagreement is a warning (count_disagree), never a failure: the line compare decides whether the files are right; this only says what the reply should show.

actual.desc: line count of each file given, in order

expected.desc: the counts in the message, in order

fileCount.desc: how many files the message names; -1 when no message

matched.desc: every file agrees with its count (true when there is nothing to compare); a short file counts as agreeing under shortOk

short.desc: per file: how many lines fewer than its count (0 when not short)

suffix.desc: " (" + label + text + ")" ready to append to a reply; "" when no message

text.desc: per file: "<count><unit>", or "<lines><unit>(<count><unit>)" when the file disagrees; the message's counts alone when no files were given

verify.record_counts.summary: Parse the per-file record counts of a start message; compare with the files' line counts

clock.desc: the run time (HH:mm[:ss] or an Excel day fraction); blank or unreadable = no window, the whole day is offered

date.desc: the run day (yyyy-MM-dd, yyyy/M/d, ...); blank = no_date

expect.desc: how many files the job has; -1 = unknown (then one is certain)

expectFallback.desc: used when expect is -1 (a worklist FileCount cell); not a number = none

label.desc: what the time is, in the set labels ("GIFT run")

namePattern.desc: regex an entry name must match (blank = any)

verify.time_candidates.notes: no_date: the job has no run day (mapping.xlsx GIFT date blank) -- put the files in by hand, or fill the date and r. Entries are compared by their own time field, to the second.

certain.desc: a run time was given and exactly the expected number of entries are in its window

dayCount.desc: entries on that day matching namePattern

picked.desc: those names when certain, else empty

sets.desc: human.pick sets: the window, then that day by hour

window.desc: the names inside the window (empty without a run time)

verify.time_candidates.summary: Listing entries around a run time: certain when the count fits, else sets to pick from

clock.desc: HH:mm[:ss[.fff]] or an Excel day fraction

format.desc: .NET format for the *Text outputs (what a page prints, e.g. yyyy/MM/dd HH:mm)

minuteTexts.desc: every minute from..to in format (browser.wait_for containsAny: ready when any of them shows)

verify.time_window.summary: Build a from/to time window around a date and a clock time
